state.decision: How GrapiX should build the dockable Workspace Manager that a 23 Nov 2026 hand-off specifies (recursive dock tree, five-zone drop targets, tab groups, saved named workspaces with session/baseline/last-known-good, floating groups, Editor and Playout catalogs).
state.what_exists_today: The Editor page is plain TypeScript and DOM, with no UI framework. It already has its own pure layout module of about 700 lines with 600 lines of tests: four fixed regions (left, centre, right, bottom), panels stacked in a region, tab groups of two or more adjacent panels, splitters between entries, collapse, a saved layout in the browser's local storage (layout version 3), and reset. It has no nested splits, no five-zone drop overlay, no named workspaces, no floating panels yet; plan rows exist for pop-out windows and named workspaces and are pending. The Playout app is a separate plain-JavaScript page with a fixed operator surface and no docking. Studios using GrapiX are often air-gapped, so nothing may need the internet. Adding an npm package needs the user's explicit approval each time. The hand-off says: keep the saved layout schema independent of any docking library, keep the panel registry and persistence separate, and that existing implementations win over new duplicates.
state.option_A: Build the whole thing in house: a new pure DockModel (recursive tree with invariants and operations), registry, presets and persistence, then a renderer on the page's own DOM, in steps, reusing and migrating the existing layout module. No new dependency.
state.option_B: Adopt the open-source Dockview library (MIT, has a framework-free core, JSON layouts and popouts) for the docking and floating behaviour, behind an adapter, and keep only the model, registry and persistence in house.
state.option_C: Own model first (pure, tested, no dependency) with a thin adapter interface, build the renderer in house for the P0 scope, and revisit a library only if floating or native pop-out windows turn out too costly to build.
state.option_migrate_replace: Replace the four-region layout with the recursive tree, and keep a reader that migrates a stored version 3 layout into the new form, so authors keep their arrangement.
state.option_migrate_keep: Keep the four-region layout as it is and add the new dock tree beside it for new features only.
state.constraints: No internet needed to dock or save. Existing tests and the user's saved layouts must keep working. Layout is interface state and must never change a scene, a revision, undo history or any playout output. The Editor and Playout need separate panel catalogs on one engine.

best_approach.instructions: Which approach should GrapiX take to build the Workspace Manager?

criteria.A: Option A: build everything in house.
criteria.B: Option B: adopt Dockview behind an adapter.
criteria.C: Option C: own model first and renderer in house, revisit a library only if floating or pop-out proves costly.

best_migration.instructions: What should happen to the existing four-region layout?

criteria.replace: Replace it with the recursive tree and migrate stored layouts.
criteria.keep: Keep it and add the new tree beside it.

library_needs_approval_first.instructions: Given that adding any npm package needs the user's explicit approval and studios are often air-gapped, is it right to start with no new dependency and ask for approval only if a library is later wanted?

criteria.true: Yes, start without a dependency and ask later if needed.
criteria.false: No, decide on the library first.

pure_model_first_is_safe.instructions: Is building and fully testing a pure dock model before touching the page's renderer a safe order of work for a layout system that must never break the Editor?

criteria.true: Yes, a tested pure model first is the safe order.
criteria.false: No, the renderer should come first.
